name: Micheál Martin
bio: Micheál Martin, born in Cork in 1960 and a history graduate of University College Cork who briefly worked as a teacher, has been Taoiseach since 23 January 2025, an office he first held from June 2020 to December 2022, and has led Fianna Fáil since January 2011. A TD for Cork South-Central since 1989 and Lord Mayor of Cork in 1992–1993, he served under Bertie Ahern and Brian Cowen as Minister for Education and Science (1997–2000), Health and Children (2000–2004), when Ireland introduced its workplace smoking ban, Enterprise, Trade and Employment (2004–2008) and Foreign Affairs (2008–2011). He left the cabinet in January 2011 after opposing Cowen in a party confidence vote, was elected party leader days later and led Fianna Fáil to its worst result in the February 2011 election, then rebuilt it in opposition. After the 2020 election he became Taoiseach in the first coalition between Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael, with the Greens, handed the office to Leo Varadkar in December 2022 as agreed, and served as Tánaiste, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Minister for Defence until January 2025. Fianna Fáil came first with 48 seats in November 2024 and he returned as Taoiseach of a Fianna Fáil–Fine Gael coalition backed by independent TDs. As of October 2026 his government holds the presidency of the Council of the EU (July–December 2026), is legislating to remove the 'triple lock' on overseas troop deployments and faces public-sector strikes over a new pay agreement, while his party leadership came under internal criticism after the 2025 presidential election and the April 2026 fuel protests.
